slides.title: Task-Based Concurrency Overview
slides.prompt: Task-based concurrency abstracts thread management. std::async runs a function asynchronously and returns a std::future, which holds the result once computed. std::promise is the provider side that sets the value for a std::future.

slides.title: Retrieving Future Result
slides.prompt: Fill in the method name used on a std::future to retrieve its value (blocking if not yet ready).
slides.codeSnippet:
std::future<int> fut = std::async([]() { return 42; });
int val = fut.___(); // Retrieves 42

slides.title: Calling future::get Multiple Times
slides.prompt: What happens if you call .get() a second time on a standard std::future object?
options: Undefined behavior / throws std::future_error because state is invalidated
slides.correctAnswer: Undefined behavior / throws std::future_error because state is invalidated

slides.title: Launch Policy Async
slides.prompt: Fill in the launch policy flag forcing std::async to execute the task on a new asynchronous thread.

slides.title: Deferred Launch Policy Behavior
slides.prompt: How does std::launch::deferred behave when passed to std::async?
options: Execution is delayed until .get() or .wait() is explicitly invoked on the returned future in the caller thread
The task runs in a background thread pool lazily
The task is cancelled if not retrieved within a timeout
It spawns an immediate detached worker thread
slides.correctAnswer: Execution is delayed until .get() or .wait() is explicitly invoked on the returned future in the caller thread

slides.title: Setting Promise Value
slides.prompt: Fill in the method on std::promise used to fulfill the promised result value.

slides.title: Shared Future Advantage
slides.prompt: What capability does std::shared_future provide over std::future?
options: It can be copied, allowing multiple threads to wait and call .get() on the same shared result
It processes values across separate processes
It consumes less memory than std::future
slides.correctAnswer: It can be copied, allowing multiple threads to wait and call .get() on the same shared result

slides.title: Obtaining Future from Promise
slides.prompt: Fill in the method on std::promise used to get its associated std::future.

slides.title: std::async Destructor Blocking Behavior
slides.prompt: What special blocking behavior occurs when a std::future returned by std::async(std::launch::async, ...) is destroyed without calling get() or wait()?
options: The destructor blocks until the asynchronous task completes execution
The task is forcefully terminated immediately
The task continues silently detached in the background
slides.correctAnswer: The destructor blocks until the asynchronous task completes execution
